 Community center wrestles with aging building; golf course weathers rainy season 
 From staff reports 
 Oct 24, 2026 
 10 hrs ago 
 0

 Aging infrastructure at the Corry Community Center and a soggy season at North Hills Golf Course are among the topics in third-quarter reports received and filed at City Council’s Oct. 19 meeting. Both reports cover July through September. 
 Corry Community Center 
 The community center’s new boiler is heating the building now that air has been bled from the pipes. However, longstanding leaks in the radiators are still present, according to the report. 
 Where the boiler leaked, the floor tiles are loose and broken, creating safety concerns. The tile is original to the building and cannot be replaced, so the center is looking into epoxy or another fix and searching for grants to pay for repairs. 
 The report discussed a goal of seeking funds to run the water lines overhead and replace the current radiators. 
 The front walkway into the building also needs repair. Broken spots will again be marked with high-visibility paint this year as renters begin using the building. 
 In the gymnasium, the center is having trouble using its remaining grant money to buy a new divider curtain. The report said a few more avenues remain to check, but the center will likely need to apply for additional funds to make the purchase. 
 The gym floor has been fully restored. To protect the new finish, the center will no longer allow food or any drink other than water in the gym. Regular rentals and sports practices are now being scheduled. 
 A kitchen upgrade paid for with Community Development Block Grant funds is expected to get under way this year. 
 The center’s Summer Recreational Program wrapped up another successful season, feeding more than 85 young people each day. Organizers plan to grow the program next year with new activities and possibly an evening meal. 
 Other community services continue at the center. Erie County has assigned four people to complete hours there through its adult community service program, and two more are working toward fine forgiveness hours. 
 The American Heart Association donated a blood pressure station, which has been used at recent events and will remain available to the public. The center also continues to work with the Erie County Health Department to distribute Narcan. 
 State Rep. Jake Banta held his annual Senior Expo at the center, which the report called a success.  
 North Hills Municipal Golf Course 
 North Hills Municipal Golf Course rebounded from a difficult start to the season, according to its quarterly report. 
 After a stretch of good weather, the report said, revenue stayed close to budget projections in the course’s four key categories: green fees, cart rentals, alcohol sales and food sales. The report said those results are good considering how much rain fell this season. 
 The course’s January-through-September budget statement, also included in the packet, shows mixed results across those categories. 
 Green fees brought in $208,212, about 14% more than the $183,100 budgeted. Alcohol sales were nearly on target at $35,759, or 99% of budget, and food sales reached $32,737, or about 90%. 
 Cart rentals fell well short. The course took in $74,196 from cart rentals, about 60% of the $122,600 budgeted. Unlimited cart pass sales were slightly ahead of budget, bringing in $28,845 against $25,000 projected. Season pass sales of $56,410 were nearly on target. 
 Overall, the course brought in $443,547 through September, about 94% of its budgeted $472,200. Expenses totaled $409,649, about 87% of budget. That left the course with net income of $33,898 for the year so far. 
 The report described the season as a tale of two halves. Spring brought very wet conditions that made the course hard to maintain. June was dry, with no substantial rain all month. Then August and September brought unseasonably heavy rain again, making daily course maintenance difficult.
